docRequirement: best-practices.md:410 binds us to a `/btw` command: "For quick questions that don't need to stay in context, use [`/btw`]... The answer appears in a dismissible overlay and never enters conversation history, so you can check a detail without growing context." The linked normative page fixes the semantics (interactive-mode.md:357-387, "Side questions with /btw"): `/btw <question>` has full visibility into the current conversation; it has NO tool access ("answer only from what is already in context"); it is a single response with no follow-up turns; it is "Available while Claude is working" and "doesn't interrupt the main turn"; it is "Low cost" because it "reuses the parent conversation's prompt cache"; earlier side questions appear as a dimmed list above the current answer and "stay out of the conversation history but remain visible in the overlay until you clear them"; a bare `/btw` reopens the overlay on the most recent exchange; and the overlay accepts `Space`/`Enter`/`Escape` (dismiss), `Up`/`Down` (scroll), `Left`/`Right` (step between answers), `c` (copy raw Markdown), `f` (fork into a new session that "inherits the parent conversation plus this question and answer as real transcript turns"), `x` (clear the earlier list).
current: Nothing named `btw` and no out-of-history answer channel of any name exists. `grep -ranE` (with `-a`, the NUL-byte trap) over packages/ apps/ docs-site/ excluding dist for `\bbtw\b`, `sideQuestion`, `side-question`, `side question`, `skipHistory`, `excludeFromHistory`, `outOfHistory` returns 0 hits; the only repo-wide hits are the doc sweep's own records under docs/superpowers/specs/. The built-in command union is apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx:17 — `PermissionMode | CustomSlashCommandId | 'agents' | 'automations' | 'compact' | 'context' | 'create-skill' | 'create-plugin' | 'export' | 'init' | 'memory' | 'model' | 'clear' | 'help' | 'subtask' | 'usage'` — and the menu list it renders is `featureCommands` at slash-command-menu.tsx:225-239; neither carries `btw`. The user-typed session-command classifier packages/shared/src/slash-commands/session-command.ts:36 admits exactly two kinds, `compact | subtask`, and its executor packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6355 `runSessionCommand` handles only those two. The model-facing `SlashCommand` tool allowlist pi-agent.ts:5402-5424 accepts only `/compact` and `/help` and throws on anything else. Because `/btw` is unknown to every layer, typed text goes down the ordinary send path: apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/FreeFormInput.tsx:1034 `submitCommand: command => onSubmit(command, undefined)` for menu items, and a plain typed line reaches `sessions:sendMessage` (packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:28) → packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:352-375 → SessionManager.sendMessage (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:15036). That path is unconditionally history-writing: SessionManager.ts:15261-15269 pushes the user message into `managed.messages` (declared SessionManager.ts:1185) and SessionManager.ts:15276-15288 calls `persistSession` + `flushSession` and emits `user_message` — the `isSessionCommand` branch at SessionManager.ts:15095 only suppresses MODEL-ONLY per-turn context, it does NOT exempt the message from the transcript, so even `/compact` and `/subtask` land in history today. The only tool-less one-shot substrate that exists is `queryLlm` (PiAgent packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7559 over the `llm_query` RPC, handled at packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:3850; ClaudeAgent packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:3140), and it takes only `request.prompt` on an ephemeral no-proxy-tool session — it carries no conversation history and reuses no parent prompt cache. There is no overlay surface, no per-session ring of ephemeral exchanges, and no session-copy fork (`/subtask`, packages/shared/src/slash-commands/subtask.ts:23, is an in-session agent fork, explicitly not a session copy).
divergence: The entire mechanism is absent, not misnamed and not narrowed: no `/btw` command id, no parser, no non-persisting answer channel, no ephemeral overlay, no earlier-answers list, no fork-from-overlay. Two of the doc's four ingredients do have substrate — a tool-less single-response model call (`queryLlm`) and an in-memory transcript to feed it (`managed.messages`) — but they are not connected, and the one path that connects a user's text to a model today is the path that writes history. So the missing piece is specifically a send route that reads the transcript, answers once with no tools, and never touches `managed.messages`/`persistSession`, plus a renderer overlay to hold the answer. Two sub-behaviours are additionally unbuildable on today's primitives without extra work: prompt-cache reuse of the parent conversation (our `queryLlm` runs an ephemeral Pi session with no history) and the `f` fork into a new session inheriting the parent transcript plus the Q/A as real turns.

userImpact: Observable and immediate. A user who follows the Claude Code guidance and types `/btw what was that config file again?` gets no `btw` entry in the inline `/` menu (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx:225-239), so the line submits as an ordinary prompt: it is appended to the transcript (SessionManager.ts:15261-15269), flushed to the session file on disk (:15276-15278), rendered as a normal user bubble, and the answer is a full tool-enabled turn that grows the context window — the exact opposite of "never enters conversation history … without growing context". If the agent is mid-turn it is worse than useless: the send is steered into the in-flight turn or queued behind it (SessionManager.ts:15155+), i.e. it derails the long-running task the doc says a side question must not interrupt. On a first message it also becomes the session title source (:15294-15320). So today the only way to ask a throwaway question is to pay for it in context, in the transcript, and possibly in the running turn.
